transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?
For the past few years I feel worn out all the time, like I’m running on empty even when I’m not doing that much. It's just a constant feeling that I can't seem to shake.

During these past few years, have you also felt down or lost interest in things most days, or is it mainly the constant exhaustion? Has there ever been a stretch of at least 2 months when you felt mostly back to normal?

It is definitely both; I feel a constant low, gray cloud and have lost interest in things I used to love, like painting, hiking, and photography. I haven't had a break from it at all—it has been steady for over three years since my company restructured. Even on vacations, I haven't felt back to normal for any stretch of time, let alone two months.

During this long period, have there been times lasting at least 2 weeks when your depression clearly got worse than your usual baseline, with symptoms like major changes in sleep or appetite, strong guilt or worthlessness, poor concentration, or thoughts of death? If so, did those symptoms happen nearly every day during that time?

I haven't really noticed any distinct two-week periods where things got significantly worse than my usual low baseline. While I definitely struggle with concentration and making mistakes at work lately, I haven't experienced major changes in my sleep or appetite, strong feelings of guilt, or any thoughts of death.

Have you ever had a period lasting several days or more when you felt unusually energized or upbeat, needed much less sleep, were more talkative, or acted more impulsively than usual? Or has your mood stayed persistently low without any such “up” periods?

No, I’ve never had any of those "up" periods or felt unusually energized or needed less sleep. My mood has just stayed persistently low, flat, and gray for the entire three-plus years since my company restructured. It's just been a steady, heavy feeling without any breaks like that.

opening_question.question: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

final_diagnosis.reason: Persistent depressed mood with low energy and anhedonia has been present continuously for over 3 years, with no symptom-free interval of 2 months, no distinct major depressive episodes superimposed on baseline, and no history of hypomanic/manic symptoms. This pattern is most consistent with dysthymia (persistent depressive disorder).
